primary_outcome: Absolute change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24 (lixisenatide two-step titration vs combined placebo)
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary endpoint was the absolute change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24.
anchor_as_printed: Lixisenatide one-/two-step once daily significantly improved HbA1c at week 24 compared with placebo (P < 0.0001)

primary_outcome: Change from baseline in mean NRS pain score at week 13 (short-term double-blind study)
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary efficacy endpoint in the short-term study was change from baseline in the mean NRS pain score at week 13.
anchor_as_printed: At week 13, the mean change from baseline in NRS score was significantly greater compared with placebo in the desvenlafaxine 200 mg (difference [95% confidence interval {CI}]: 1.10 [0.50 to 1.70]; P<0.001) and 400 mg groups (0.91 [95% CI: 0.23 to 1.59]; P=0.027); differences from placebo were not statistically significant for the 50 mg (0.58 [95% CI: -0.08 to 1.25]) and 100 mg (0.59 [95% CI: -0.03 to 1.21]) groups
notes: paper reports a 13-week RCT plus an open-label extension; the meta label (50% pain reduction) is a secondary responder outcome; four dose arms vs placebo

primary_outcome: Change in pain intensity from baseline to endpoint on an 11-point NRS
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary efficacy measure was the changes in the pain intensity from baseline to endpoint measured on an 11-point NRS (numeric rating scale).
anchor_as_printed: at the end of weeks four and eight, the decrease in the mean pain NRS score was significantly greater in patients taking CoQ10 + pregabalin than in those taking placebo + pregabalin (p value = 0.01 and < 0.001, respectively)
notes: abstract gives P values only; take the NRS means from the results table in phase 5; the meta labelled 50% pain reduction (a responder secondary); Springer PDF saved by Zaid

primary_outcome: Reduction in VAS pain score of more than 50% within 4 weeks (responder)
primary_outcome_source: Methods: Primary outcome was a reduction in VAS score within a 4-week period, with a greater than 50% reduction compared with the baseline considered clinically significant.
anchor_as_printed: Thirteen patients from the experimental arm achieved an at least 50% reduction in VAS score, compared with none of the placebo patients (NNT = 1.2, 95% CI, 2-1; ARR = 0.87, 95% CI, 0.55-0.96; P < 0.001)
notes: n = 30; no registration id in the PDF; Clin J Pain PDF saved by Zaid

primary_outcome: Endpoint mean pain score from daily pain diaries (11-point NRS)
primary_outcome_source: Methods: the primary efficacy measure was endpoint mean pain score (MPS) from daily pain diaries (11-point scale).
anchor_as_printed: Pregabalin-treated patients had lower MPS than controls (mean difference, -1.28; p <.001)
notes: primary safety parameter also defined (nerve conduction)

primary_outcome: Reduction from baseline in pain scores on the VAS and Likert scale over the 6-week maintenance period (ITT-E, LOCF)
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary measure of efficacy was the reduction from baseline in pain scores on the VAS and the Likert scale in the ITT-E population, using the mean score for the 6-week maintenance period with last-observation-carried-forward imputation.
anchor_as_printed: Pain scores on both the visual analog scale and the Likert scale decreased more for the zonisamide group compared with the placebo group, regardless of whether the comparison was made for the intent-to-treat population, the population that entered the maintenance phase, or the completer population, but these differences did not reach statistical significance
notes: pilot, zonisamide vs placebo; no registration; abstract gives no numbers, take from the results tables in phase 5; Wiley PDF saved by Zaid

primary_outcome: Change from baseline in self-reported mean weekly pain intensity over 24 weeks
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary outcome was the efficacy of botulinum toxin A versus placebo, measured as the change from baseline in self-reported mean weekly pain intensity over the course of 24 weeks from the first administration.
anchor_as_printed: Botulinum toxin A reduced pain intensity over 24 weeks compared with placebo (adjusted effect estimate -0.77, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.59; p<0.0001)
notes: the meta labelled 50% pain reduction (a secondary); Lancet Neurol PDF saved by Zaid, appendix by curl

primary_outcome: Mean change in 24-hour proteinuria from baseline over 24 weeks, telitacicept vs placebo
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary end point was the mean change in 24-hour proteinuria from baseline over a 24-week medication period.
anchor_as_printed: Telitacicept 240 mg therapy reduced mean proteinuria by 49% from baseline (change in proteinuria vs. placebo, -0.88; 95% confidence interval, -1.57 to -0.20; P = 0.013), whereas telitacicept 160 mg reduced it by 25% (-0.29; 95% confidence interval, -0.95 to 0.37; P = 0.389)
notes: REPLACEMENT for protect (next in-set trial in the meta table order after a conference abstract was skipped); phase 2, three arms; KI Reports open access, fetched in Chrome, supplement by curl

primary_outcome: Change from baseline in 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months, felzartamab vs placebo
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in 24-hour urine protein:creatinine ratio (UPCR) at 9 months.
anchor_as_printed: Treatment with felzartamab versus placebo led to rapid (within 3-6 months) reduction in least-squares mean UPCR sustained at nine months (placebo, -5.7%; 2-dose, -12.5%; 5-dose, -12.8%; 9-dose, -29.5%; part 2, -44.8%)
notes: REPLACEMENT for align; phase 2a with several dose arms and a part 2; abstract gives arm percentages, no CI; Kidney Int open access, fetched in Chrome

primary_outcome: Change from baseline in average pain intensity (BPI, 0-10 NRS) over 25 weeks, M1-rTMS and DLPFC-rTMS vs sham
primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary outcome measure was the mean change from baseline over the course of 25 weeks (Group x Time interaction) in average pain intensity from the BPI (scored on a 0-10 NRS).

primary_outcome: Clinical and instrumented outcomes (KT-1000 arthrometer, pivot shift, IKDC, Lysholm) of isolated ACL vs combined ACL and anterolateral ligament reconstruction at a mean 27 months (no single primary is designated)
primary_outcome_source: Abstract: the outcomes of anatomic ACL reconstruction with and without anterolateral ligament reconstruction were compared (see the Purpose statement in the abstract).

notes: REPLACEMENT for el-azab-2023 (next in-set trial in the meta table order); no registration id in the PDF; AJSM PDF saved by Zaid; no supplements listed

primary_outcome: End-tidal oxygen fraction after 2.5 and 5.0 min of preoxygenation (two primary outcomes), high-flow nasal cannula vs face mask with PEEP
